chunks: And in the narration of al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:
The magician among the Muslims is to be killed, and the magician among the disbelievers is not to be killed.
It was said: O Messenger of Allah, why is the magician among the disbelievers not killed?
He said: Because shirk is greater than magic, and because magic and shirk are joined together.

key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the Muslims; those belonging to the Muslim community
key_terms.سَاحِرُ: a magician; one who practices sihr
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ: is to be killed; subject to execution

ai.seo_question: Why does this hadith say the magician among the disbelievers is not executed while the magician among Muslims is?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling concerning the magician among Muslims and distinguishes it from the magician among the disbelievers. It also links magic with shirk, stating that shirk is graver and that the two are closely associated.
